content.title: How UCLA knocked off Texas to reach women's NCAA Tournament championship game
content.text: The Bruins held off a late Longhorns rally to win the Final Four game 51-44.UCLA will play for the national title for the first in program history on Sunday. Getty Images UCLA takes down TexasUCLA is headed to the national championship game for the first time in program history after beating Texas 51-44 in the women’s NCAA Tournament Final Four.The Bruins will face another SEC program, South Carolina, on Sunday for the title. UCLA center Lauren Betts had 16 points, 11 rebounds and three blocked shots, including a huge block on Madison Booker late in the game with the Bruins leading by three points.Share your thoughts on the game: live@theathletic.comLast time a Big Ten team won the title? Getty ImagesOne of the newest members of the Big Ten, UCLA will attempt to make history for the conference in the national championship on Sunday.The last Big Ten team to win it all? Purdue in 1999. The 20th century!Since then, Purdue, Michigan State and Iowa have reached the title game but lost in their respective appearances.On Sunday, it will be up to the Big Ten tournament champion to claim the conference's first title of this century.Readers' views on UCLA winBelow are some of your postgame reader thoughts on tonight’s UCLA and Texas semifinal.UCLA avenges regular-season loss to Texas Getty ImagesThe Final Four's Big Ten-SEC matchup was more familiar than the typical interconference matchup.Texas and UCLA played on Nov. 26, and the Longhorns won by double digits. At the time, Texas was No. 4 team in the nation, and UCLA ranked No. 3.To the surprise of very few, the game featured more points than the low-scoring Final Four rematch. Texas secured a 76-65 win with 26 points from Rori Harmon and 16 points from Madison Booker. Lauren Betts, the Bruins' leading scorer in the Final Four, posted just eight points in the teams' first meeting.UCLA's reward is a title game matchup against another SEC team, South Carolina, but the Bruins will face the Gamecocks for the first time this season.Bruins get a title shot UCLA will play for the national title for the first time in program history on Sunday against South Carolina. So how did the Bruins get past Texas to earn that matchup?Our Grace Raynor breaks it all down here.Betts' Final Four showing continues dominant tournament run Imagn ImagesUCLA's Lauren Betts was the most impactful and effective player on the court in the Bruins' matchup against the Texas Longhorns. Betts' heroics are nothing new. Here's how she has performed through this year's NCAA Tournament:First round against California Baptist: 22 points, 9-15 FG, 10 rebounds, 1 blockSecond round against Oklahoma State: 35 points, 15-19 FG, 9 rebounds, 1 blockSweet 16 against Minnesota: 16 points, 7-9 FG, 5 rebounds, 5 blocksElite Eight against Duke: 23 points, 9-14 FG, 10 rebounds, 5 blocksFinal Four against Texas: 16 points, 7-10 FG, 11 rebounds, 3 blocksSouth Carolina-UCLA history Getty ImagesSouth Carolina and UCLA have faced off five times in their history, with South Carolina winning four times.2024-25: UCLA 77-622022-23: South Carolina 59-432022-23: South Carolina 73-642016-17: South Carolina 66-572015-16: South Carolina 65-68When is the title game? Getty ImagesSunday's national title game between UCLA and South Carolina will tip off at 3:30 p.m. ET. UCLA wins despite 23 turnovers Getty ImagesUCLA earned its spot in the national championship in a 51-44 win over Texas, but one aspect the Bruins will look to clean up on Sunday is protecting the basketball.The Bruins committed 23 turnovers — 11 more than Texas committed — and that carelessness allowed the Longhorns to turn a game UCLA almost led wire-to-wire into a nail-biter late. Nineteen of those 23 turnovers came from the Bruins' starters, and six came in the final quarter with UCLA attempting to close the game out.UCLA benefited from the Longhorns failing to take full advantage of those turnovers (Texas turned those turnovers into 15 points), and the Bruins can't count on South Carolina also failing to capitalize.Staley on facing UCLA Getty ImagesDawn Staley to Scott Van Pelt just now on "SportsCenter" on facing UCLA: 💬 “It’s the same kind of approach, we’ll probably be the underdogs in the next game. Same approach, once you get to this point in the season, you’re going to do whatever is necessary in order for us to win, continue to belief, continue to lock in, continue to execute.”Close on limiting Booker Getty ImagesMadison Booker finished 3-of-23 from the floor tonight.Here is UCLA coach Cori Close on limiting the Texas star: 💬 “It was the focus of our group to just make her catches more uncomfortable. … We wanted her catches to happen at 17 (instead of 12) feet. … Madison Booker is an incredible player, I’ve watched her with USA Basketball and obviously her career at Texas.”Final stats Getty ImagesFG:Texas: 20-of-65UCLA: 18-of-443FG:Texas: 2-of-9UCLA: 4-of-13Rebounds: Texas: 36UCLA: 37Assists:Texas: 11UCLA: 13Steals:Texas: 14UCLA: 5Turnovers:Texas: 12UCLA: 23Points in the paint: Texas: 24UCLA: 24Largest lead: Texas: 2UCLA: 13UCLA-Texas heated up in final quarter Getty ImagesAt the start of the third quarter, UCLA coach Cori Close apologized to fans watching the UCLA-Texas semifinal matchup for its terrible shooting efficiency and "rugby match" physicality.But fans and viewers were rewarded for their patience in a final quarter that saw Texas nearly complete its rally from a 13-point deficit and cut UCLA's lead to a possession in the final minutes. UCLA ultimately won 51-44, and maybe more impressively considering the flow of the game to that point, it exceeded 50 points.Here's how the combined quarter point totals compared:First quarter: 20 pointsSecond quarter: 17 pointsThird quarter: 22 pointsFourth quarter: 36 pointsUCLA one win away Getty ImagesUCLA achieved program history. It’s the first time the Bruins women’s basketball program advances to the national title game.Previously, UCLA was 0-1 in the women’s Final Four. Now 1-1 after avenging last year’s loss to UConn in the semis. The Bruins are one win away from a maiden national championship. Final scoring leaders Getty ImagesBelow are the final scoring leaders for Texas and UCLA:Texas: Kyla Oldacre (11 points, 5-of-10 FG)UCLA: Lauren Betts (16 points, 7-of-10 FG)Cori Close: 'We stayed connected' Getty ImagesUCLA coach Cori Close admitted after the game that it wasn’t the prettiest basketball, but she was proud of her players for finding a way to grind out the win.💬 “It wasn’t the sport I thought I was coaching. It was more rugby than it was basketball.”💬 “There were ups and downs, but I thought we stayed connected, and I thought we were pretty darn tough on the defensive end so we can weather the storm on the defensive end.”Lauren Betts: 'I wanted to win this for my team' Getty ImagesAfter the game, Lauren Betts spoke about finally advancing to the national championship and, of course, that epic block. 💬 “I just wanted to win it so bad for this team. We work so hard, it’s just execution. When you work so hard in practice and … you’re consistent every day, great things happen."On the block: 💬 “My instincts. Just playing defense, protecting the basket. It’s what I do, helping my team out. We just earned another day with each other, and I’m so happy. … This group is amazing, and I love my team so much.”Betts turns back to her team and yells, “We’re playing in the national championship!”Double-double for BettsIt’s no secret that this was an ugly basketball game. But Lauren Betts once again found a way to lead her team to victory with a gutsy effort.Betts recorded a double-double with 16 points and 11 rebounds. She also made the critical block in the dying seconds with UCLA up three, en route to victory. She is playing for her first national title. What a career she’s had with the Bruins. National title game setA fascinating women’s national championship game awaits.UCLA versus South Carolina. The Bruins trying to win their first national title in program history. South Carolina going for its fourth. A lot on the line in Phoenix on Sunday. UCLA defeats Texas to advance to title game Getty ImagesFINAL – UCLA 51, Texas 44UCLA is headed to its first national championship game!Lauren Betts tallied 16 points and 11 rebounds, but the game's iconic play is her resounding block in the final minute that both denied Madison Booker's reverse layup attempt and directed the ball back to the Bruins. What a defensive effort from UCLA and what poise in the final moments.The Bruins will play the South Carolina Gamecocks on Sunday for the title.
